security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and relative documentation links. Two risks remain: the Resend shell example lacks safe handling for supplied values, and the save filename is derived from a flow or goal without a stated sanitization rule.

remediation.issue: The Resend activation example places supplied values into a shell command.
remediation.suggestion: Provide a wrapper that passes validated values as structured arguments, or require strict allowlists and shell-safe quoting for every supplied value.

remediation.issue: The save path includes a user-derived flow or goal name.
remediation.suggestion: Generate the filename from a slug allowlist, reject path separators and dot segments, and verify the resolved path remains inside the memory directory.

content.value_statement: Email teams often lack a clear lifecycle map and send too frequently. This skill creates flow plans with timing, exits, and safeguards before copywriting begins.
actual_capabilities: Maps welcome, cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, re-engagement, and cold-outbound flows.
Defines triggers, delays, goals, branches, and exit conditions for each flow.
Sets global send caps, quiet hours, and fatigue guardrails.
Creates an engagement-decay and sunset path for inactive recipients.
Produces a SEND N dimension score with notes for lifecycle coverage.
Prepares a handoff summary for email copywriting and quality review.
limitations: It does not write individual email subjects, bodies, or calls to action.
It does not calculate final EQS scores or enforce unsubscribe vetoes.
It requires reliable trigger and segment details for an implementation-ready plan.
It does not replace legal, consent, or suppression-list review.

use_cases.title: Plan a welcome journey
use_cases.description: Create a triggered onboarding sequence with progressive goals, timing, and exits for new subscribers.

use_cases.title: Reduce abandoned-cart friction
use_cases.description: Design a cart recovery flow with discount branches, purchase exits, and frequency limits.

use_cases.title: Control list fatigue
use_cases.description: Set cadence rules, quiet hours, and sunset thresholds across overlapping campaigns.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: welcome flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a three-step welcome flow for a skincare brand. The trigger is newsletter signup. Include timing, goal, and exit conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: cart recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an abandoned-cart sequence for our online store. Use three steps over five days, an exit on purchase, and a discount branch.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: cadence governance
prompt_templates.prompt: Map our welcome, cart, post-purchase, and re-engagement flows. Set global caps, quiet hours, fatigue rules, and a sunset policy.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: B2B outbound lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cold-outbound sequence for mid-market IT buyers. Include reply exits, role-based branches, send windows, and a SEND N score.

output_examples.input: Design a welcome flow for a subscription fitness app.
output: Step 1: send immediately with setup guidance; exit on first workout logged.
Step 2: send after two days to inactive users with a workout recommendation.
Guardrail: maximum two lifecycle emails in seven days.

output_examples.input: Create an abandoned-cart sequence with a discount branch.
output: Trigger: cart inactive for one hour.
Step 1: send after one hour with cart reminder; exit on purchase.
Step 2: send after 24 hours; show discount only to non-purchasers.
Sunset: stop after step three or an unsubscribe, bounce, or suppression event.

best_practices: Confirm the trigger source and target segment before finalizing enrollment rules.
Use explicit conversion, reply, bounce, and unsubscribe exits in every relevant flow.
Apply one global send cap across flows to prevent overlapping messages.
anti_patterns: Do not send all recipients through the same flow without lifecycle segmentation.
Do not continue a sequence after a conversion, reply, unsubscribe, or bounce.
Do not treat a re-engagement branch as consent to resume mailing indefinitely.

faq.question: Does this skill write email copy?
faq.answer: No. It designs the flow structure. Use an email copywriting skill for subjects, bodies, and calls to action.

faq.question: Can it plan an abandoned-cart campaign?
faq.answer: Yes. It can define cart triggers, delays, purchase exits, discount branches, and frequency safeguards.

faq.question: Can it send emails through my provider?
faq.answer: It can document an optional Resend activation workflow, but sending requires your confirmation and valid consent controls.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the lifecycle goal, trigger event, target segment, current flows, and any cadence or complaint data.

faq.question: Does it handle unsubscribe compliance?
faq.answer: It includes unsubscribe exits in flow design, but a separate quality or compliance review should verify implementation.

faq.question: Can it design win-back programs?
faq.answer: It can add a light re-engagement branch. Closed-loop re-consent programs for lapsed cohorts are outside its scope.
